evidence.text: The Q3 report is the promised venue for an updated cost estimate on the Carolina/Victoria preparation projects (previously 'up to $130 million'), and the LOI adjusts the number of consideration shares for CAPEX. An overrun therefore lands directly on what VTURA holders receive. The 2026-10-07 statement that the new DNB financing fully funds the company until a January 2027 start limits the overrun tail, so the net risk is small and slightly negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior capex re-estimate under the LOI. The 2026-04-02 capex and financing update (which set the $130m figure and the $75m tap) is not in the results-day history. The closest observable is 2026-08-31, when Fearnley cut its target to NOK 37 from 39 after Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: The estimate does not exist publicly yet; the company said it will publish it in this report ('the Company expects to announce an updated estimate in its third quarter report'). How the LOI's CAPEX adjustment converts an overrun into fewer consideration shares has not been published, so the market cannot price the mapping. If an overrun were priced, VTURA would trade at a persistently wider spread than its post-LOI median (~10.7%). It is at 14.1%, which is consistent with but not proof of this.
